ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, the line $l_{1}$ passes through points $A(1,0)$ and $B(0,2)$. What is the analytical expression of line $l_{1}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.title: MM-Math open-ended problem
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, the line $l_{1}$ passes through points $A(1,0)$ and $B(0,2)$. What is the analytical expression of line $l_{1}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Let the equation of line $l_{1}$ be $y=kx+b$. According to the problem, we have \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} k+b=0, \\ b=2. \end{array} \right. \] Solving these equations, we find \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} k=-2, \\ b=2. \end{array} \right. \] $\therefore$ The equation of line $l_{1}$ is \boxed{y=-2x+2}.

Because point B(0,2) is on the y-axis, the y-intercept of the line is 2. Substitute into the slope-intercept form y=mx+b, obtaining the analytic expression of l1 as y=-2x+2.
